sections.title: The Lord's Judgment Against Israel
observations: Micah begins his prophecy by declaring the coming judgment of the Lord against Israel and Judah. He emphasizes the seriousness of this judgment by invoking the imagery of God coming down from His holy temple to witness the sins of His people.

The mention of the mountains melting like wax before the Lord illustrates the power and majesty of God, as well as the totality of His judgment. This imagery serves to remind the people of their unfaithfulness and the consequences that follow.

sections.title: The Reasons for Judgment
observations: Micah identifies specific sins that have led to God's judgment, including idolatry and injustice. The people have turned away from the covenant relationship with God, leading to moral decay and social injustice.
The reference to Samaria and Jerusalem highlights the central cities of Israel and Judah, indicating that the judgment will affect both the northern and southern kingdoms.

sections.title: The Lamentation of Micah
observations: Micah expresses his deep sorrow over the impending judgment. His lamentation reflects the heart of a true prophet who cares for his people and desires their repentance.
This section serves as a call for the people to recognize the gravity of their situation and to turn back to God before it is too late.

sections.title: The Consequences of Sin
observations: The chapter concludes with a description of the devastation that will come as a result of the people's sins. Micah uses vivid imagery to portray the destruction of cities and the suffering of the people.
This serves as a warning to the people of Israel and Judah about the seriousness of their actions and the reality of God's judgment.

importantVerses.commentary: Hear, you peoples, all of you; pay attention, O earth, and all that is in it, and let the Lord God be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple!
All her carved images shall be beaten to pieces, all her wages shall be burned with fire, and all her idols I will lay waste.

questions: What specific sins does Micah highlight that led to God's judgment?
How does the imagery used by Micah enhance our understanding of God's character and His response to sin?
In what ways can we apply the lessons from Micah's lamentation to our own lives and communities today?
